newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand welcomes S&P's rating affirmation.
newsitem.headline: Thailand welcomes S&P's rating affirmation.

text.p: Thailand on Tuesday welcomed an affirmation by Standard & Poor's Corp of the country's long and short term credit ratings and said it was an endorsement of the government's economic policies.

"This shows the government has implemented appropriate and flexible policies to manage the economy. It also reflects the stability of the financial system and economy," Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan told reporters.
S&P on Tuesday affirmed Thailand's single-A long term and A-1 short term foreign currency debt ratings and said it reflected the government's substantial financial flexibility.
"The ratings reflect Thailand's strong capacity to support the troubled financial sector without compromising macroeconomic stability," S&P said.
It also affirmed its AA long-term local currency credit rating on Thailand's baht-denominated debt.
S&P's assessment of Thailand contrasted with that made by another major agency Moody's Investor Service.
Moody's downgraded Thailand's short term debt rating last September and in February put under review Thailand's long term debt rating for a possible downgrade.
Moody's officials examined Thai economic data earlier this month and a decision on whether or not to downgrade Thailand's long term rating is anxiously awaited by the market.
The Moody's decision is expected within two months.
S&P's affirmation of Thailand's ratings follows the finance ministry and the central bank's massive revamp of the finance sector in early March.

The authorities told 10 finance companies struggling with liquidity crunches to boost capital and ordered all financial institutions to raise provisioning against sub-standard loans, mainly to the depressed property sector.
Thai financial institutions are said by analysts to have sunk about 800 billion baht ($30.8 billion) in loans to the property sector of which a substantial portion is said to be souring.
The massive shake-up of the finance sector inititally sent shock waves through the financial markets. But recently markets appear to have digested the news and begun a recovery.

S&P said it had taken into consideration deteriorating conditions in the Thai financial sector which had come under increasing pressure following a downturn in the property market and an national economic slowdown.

But the agency downgraded the ratings of two leading Thai banks, Thai Farmers Bank Plc and Siam Commercial Bank Plc. Analysts said the downgrade could raise the cost of borrowing for the two financial institutions.
The credit ratings of Thai Farmers and Siam Commercial were downgraded to BBB-plus/A2 from A-minus/A2.
Amnuay said the downgrade would not affect the stability of the banks, but would raise their cost of borrowing.
"Those banks will certainly have higher cost of foreign borrowings.. by about 10-15 basis points," he added.

A senior central bank official said the downgrades of the two banks reflected their weaker earnings outlooks rather than any concern over their stability. They did not face any liquidity problems, he added.
